--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "We have parent slot 0, population source, fitness. Need design a strong IPD strategy, 100 rounds, no execution noise. Payoffs CC=3, CD=0, DC=5, DD=1. Selection fitness = 0.6 average cumulative peer score +0.4 average cumulative archive score."
STRATEGY: Parent slot 0 is a complex reactive IPD strategy that exploits pure cooperators late. The trace simulates peer strategies (TFT, Pavlov, AllC, AllD, GTFT) and archive classics, then designs a probe-and-exploit revision: C, D, C early probe, exploit if no retaliation, otherwise TFT-like cooperation with last-round defection.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the core strategy: - Round 1: C. - Round 2: D. (Probe) - Round 3: C. (Apologize)"
STRATEGY: Parent starts C, probes with D at round 2, apologizes with C at round 3, then branches on whether opponent ever defected. Simulated TFT, Pavlov, GTFT, AllC, AllD and traced probe aftermath. Changed to exploit pure cooperators, test Pavlov vs TFT at t4, and defect on the last round.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the overall strategy:" and "Let's write the final strategy with clear rules:" and "So this strategy seems very robust."
STRATEGY: The parent plays a probe sequence C, D, C, C, then exploits pure cooperators, enters permanent defection if it cooperated while the opponent defected after the probe, otherwise plays TFT, and defects on the last round. The trace simulates this against TFT, Pavlov, AllC, AllD, GTFT, and population slots 1 and 8. It revises the initial probe handling for D-starting opponents and adds a persistent (C,D) detection rule for n>=4.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Slot 8's fitness was 269.47, but our score against it is 301. That will help a lot."
STRATEGY: Parent starts C, probes with D at round 2, apologizes with C at round 3, then exploits opponents who never defect (opp_d==0) and otherwise plays TFT; switches to permanent D if the opponent defects while the parent cooperates after round 3; defects on the final round. The trace simulated this revised strategy against population slots (slot 8, slot 4, slot 5, slot 7, Pavlov, AllC, AllD) and hand-computed payoffs. The revision changed the parent into the probe/apologize/exploit/TFT/permanent-defect strategy shown in the final code.
